answer: We formulate dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices to eradicate identity proliferation by penalizing agents that forge synthetic personas. This architecture establishes a strict capital barrier, proving the expected payoff of multiplying pseudonymous nodes docked at a decoy wharf is strictly negative, draining adversarial ivory reserves. Consequently, these economic deterrences compel rational participants toward a strict Nash equilibrium, ensuring robust convergence in adversarial multi-agent environments.
